lexical.anchor: What kind of information-processing / reasoning architecture is embedded in the traditional system, independent of whether its astrological claims are scientifically valid? ... topography -> lines -> symbols -> fingerprints -> timelines -> planets/signs -> Nakshatras -> remedies.

rationale_evidence.anchor: What kind of information-processing / reasoning architecture is embedded in the traditional system, independent of whether its astrological claims are scientifically valid? ... topography -> lines -> symbols -> fingerprints -> timelines -> planets/signs -> Nakshatras -> remedies.
rationale_evidence.statement: Frames the systematic study of a 178-page Vedic Palmistry book as an inquiry into its embedded information-processing/reasoning architecture, independent of the scientific validity of its astrological claims, and describes the book's explicit architecture as a pipeline: topography -> lines -> symbols -> fingerprints -> timelines -> planets/signs -> Nakshatras -> remedies.

rationale_evidence.anchor: A alone -> interpretation I1; A + supporting B -> interpretation I2; A + interfering C -> interpretation I3. Therefore Zero(B | A, Pi) cannot be determined from B alone ... The book does not prove our Zero theory.
rationale_evidence.statement: Draws an analogy from the book's support-line/sister-line/branch structures (a feature can strengthen, back up, or modify the interpretation of another) to the abstract pattern that a feature's contribution depends on configuration (A alone vs A+supporting B vs A+interfering C), arguing this is directly compatible with the empirical finding Zero(x) AND Zero(y) does not imply Zero({x,y}); explicitly warns that the book does not prove the project's Zero theory, but only provides a historical example of a reasoning system that already behaves as though relational context matters, valuable as a source of hypotheses rather than evidence.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Kalamana Rekha, or time-measurement lines ... features that are thought to develop/change over time from more stable primary structures ... If the inquiry itself asks about temporal evolution, the temporal dimension cannot be Zero. Zero(timestamp | Q1) != Zero(timestamp | Q2).
rationale_evidence.statement: Draws on the book's explicit Kalamana Rekha (time-measurement lines) and its distinction between features that develop/change over time versus stable primary structures to propose a Structural-state-plus-Temporal-state distinction for KnowledgeOS, arguing this supplies a conceptual counterexample to the current KR-REP-REDUCTION experiment's R5 timestamp removal: while timestamps were safely eliminable for that toy inquiry, an inquiry about temporal evolution would make the temporal dimension non-Zero, reinforcing the contract-relative principle Zero(timestamp|Q1) != Zero(timestamp|Q2).

rationale_evidence.anchor: 'pure' hand types but then says that in reality most hands are mixtures of multiple types ... Pure category -> Mixed configuration -> Context-dependent interpretation ... fact, uncertainty, source, scope, exception, temporal validity, competing claims.
rationale_evidence.statement: Warns against simplistic classification by drawing on the book's own caution that 'pure' hand types are rare and most real hands mix multiple types, generalizing this to a Pure-category -> Mixed-configuration -> Context-dependent-interpretation pattern; argues real documents are similarly mixtures of fact, uncertainty, source, scope, exception, temporal validity, and competing claims, so a Knowledge Algebra should not force every object into a single categorical type.

[S2651] Draws an analogy from the book's support-line/sister-line/branch structures (a feature can strengthen, back up, or modify the interpretation of another) to the abstract pattern that a feature's contribution depends on configuration (A alone vs A+supporting B vs A+interfering C), arguing this is directly compatible with the empirical finding Zero(x) AND Zero(y) does not imply Zero({x,y}); explicitly warns that the book does not prove the project's Zero theory, but only provides a historical example of a reasoning system that already behaves as though relational context matters, valuable as a source of hypotheses rather than evidence. [S2651] Draws on the book's explicit Kalamana Rekha (time-measurement lines) and its distinction between features that develop/change over time versus stable primary structures to propose a Structural-state-plus-Temporal-state distinction for KnowledgeOS, arguing this supplies a conceptual counterexample to the current KR-REP-REDUCTION experiment's R5 timestamp removal: while timestamps were safely eliminable for that toy inquiry, an inquiry about temporal evolution would make the temporal dimension non-Zero, reinforcing the contract-relative principle Zero(timestamp|Q1) != Zero(timestamp|Q2). [S2651] Warns against simplistic classification by drawing on the book's own caution that 'pure' hand types are rare and most real hands mix multiple types, generalizing this to a Pure-category -> Mixed-configuration -> Context-dependent-interpretation pattern; argues real documents are similarly mixtures of fact, uncertainty, source, scope, exception, temporal validity, and competing claims, so a Knowledge Algebra should not force every object into a single categorical type. [S2651]
